# 救疾經

**ID:** T2878
**Volume:** T85
**Category:** 敦煌寫本部類
**Original Category:** 疑似部
**Juans:** 1
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T2878

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle protective and healing apocryphon, set — like [KR6u0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6u/KR6u0001) (*Hùshēnmìng jīng*) — at the twin *śāla* trees on the eve of the Buddha's *parinirvāṇa*. The Buddha exhorts the assembly to spread the text after his death in order to bring healing to a corrupt world; subsequent passages describe the encounter with three ulcerated and disfigured beggars whose plight prompts the Buddha's healing teaching. The text is preserved with substantial lacunae (visible as 「□」 boxes), and is collated in the Tàishō against multiple manuscript witnesses (甲, 乙).

**Abstract**

T85n2878 is a Dūnhuáng manuscript apocryphon. It belongs to the same protective-healing genre as the *Hùshēnmìng jīng* cluster ([KR6u0001](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6u/KR6u0001)/0002), the *Yánshòumìng jīng* ([KR6u0024](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6u/KR6u0024)), and the *Xùmìng jīng* ([KR6u0025](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6u/KR6u0025)), all of which deploy the *parinirvāṇa* setting to authorise a short, talismanic Buddha-utterance for averting illness, prolonging life, and managing demonic interference. The text is registered as 偽 in catalogues from the Suí period onward. Modern scholarship treats it as a representative case of Northern-Dynasties to Táng "healing-cult" apocrypha; Christine Mollier (2008) has shown how this stratum overlaps in iconography and ritual lexicon with Daoist *jiùjí* and *yánshòu* talismanic scripture-traditions.
